steps.title: Start with a silicon wafer
steps.detail: A 300 mm single-crystal silicon wafer, polished flat to a few atoms.

steps.title: Grow the Si/SiGe superlattice
steps.detail: Alternating layers of silicon-germanium and silicon are grown epitaxially, three of each. The SiGe layers are placeholders that will later be etched away.

steps.title: Pattern the dummy gate
steps.detail: Polysilicon dummy gates are printed at the contacted gate pitch (~45 nm) with EUV lithography and etched.

steps.title: Add gate spacers
steps.detail: A thin dielectric film is deposited conformally and etched back to leave spacers on the gate walls.

steps.title: Etch the source/drain cavities
steps.detail: The stack is etched away beside the spacers, down to the substrate.

steps.title: Indent the SiGe layers
steps.detail: A selective etch recesses only the SiGe under the spacers, leaving the silicon sheets sticking out.

steps.title: Form inner spacers
steps.detail: Dielectric fills the indents. These inner spacers isolate the future metal gate from the source/drain.

steps.title: Grow source and drain
steps.detail: Phosphorus-doped silicon (nFET) or boron-doped SiGe (pFET) grows epitaxially from the exposed sheet ends.

steps.title: Fill and planarize
steps.detail: An inter-layer dielectric fills the gaps and is polished down to the top of the dummy gate.

steps.title: Remove the dummy gate
steps.detail: The polysilicon placeholder is etched out, opening a trench to the superlattice.

steps.title: Release the nanosheets
steps.detail: A highly selective etch removes the SiGe between the sheets. The silicon sheets now hang free between the source and drain.

steps.title: Wrap high-k and metal gate
steps.detail: HfO₂ and work-function metals coat every sheet surface, then metal fills the gaps: the gate is all around.

steps.title: Contacts and wiring
steps.detail: Trench contacts land on source/drain, then a dozen or more copper layers wire transistors together.

steps.title: Optional: backside power
steps.detail: The wafer is bonded to a carrier, flipped, thinned to ~µm, and power rails are built on the back (PowerVia, Super Power Rail).
